A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same random-feature ensemble study. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial changes in scope, organization, and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic Gaussian and binarized CIFAR-10/MNIST experiments, plus CNN, ResNet18, and transformer ensemble results.

after.justification: V2 retains original synthetic Gaussian and binarized CIFAR-10/MNIST experiments, including numerical comparisons with theoretical predictions and supplementary classification analyses.

M1.justification: The RFRR procedure retains independently sampled features, separate ridge fits, and averaged predictions. V2 expands the objective and kernel-limit exposition; its corresponding weight and prediction rescaling does not change the predictor.

E1.justification: V2 retains synthetic Gaussian regression and binarized CIFAR-10/MNIST, but removes deep-network CIFAR-10 classification and language modeling. The removed language experiment is labeled C4 in v1 Section 6/Figure 5 and WikiText2 in Appendix E.1; the entire NLP branch disappears.

E2.justification: The retained RFRR comparisons use the same single-model and ensemble configurations, including score-averaging and majority-vote variants. Newly cited sketched and subsampled ensemble methods are discussed as related work, not evaluated as additional comparators.

E3.justification: V2 removes the deep-network evaluation protocols: parameter-matched architectures, maximal-update parameterization, richness and weight-decay sweeps, augmentation/early-stopping controls, and 5,000-step online transformer training. The retained RFRR sample sizes, feature budgets, metrics, and experimental procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1's deep-network sensitivity analyses across richness and weight decay, including CNN training without augmentation or early stopping, disappear with Figures S8-S10. The RFRR bias-variance, classification-rule, spectral-fitting, and bound-tightness analyses in Figures S1-S7 are retained.

E5.justification: The retained experiments preserve their uncertainty-reporting practices: means and standard deviations over 50 trials in Figures 1/S3 and 10 trials in Figures 2/S1/S4. No new seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 removes the CNN/ResNet18 accuracy curves, transformer loss curves, and associated sensitivity results from v1 Figures 5 and S8-S10. The retained RFRR numerical results and scaling trends persist; the new Figure 3 is a schematic rather than additional experimental evidence.

T1.justification: The main theorems, scaling laws, and overparameterized expansion are retained. V2 distinguishes deterministic-equivalence regimes and expands the proof rationale. It also corrects Df_2 < Df_2 to Df_2 < Df_1 in v1 B.1/v2 C.1 and Var_z^2 to Var_z in v1 C.10/v2 D.10.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion withdraw the claimed empirical extension to deep feature-learning ensembles. V2 centers its contributions on RFRR optimality and near-optimality conditions in both parameterization regimes, promoting an overparameterized result already present in v1 rather than introducing that result anew.

C2.justification: V1's empirically supported rule of thumb for deep ensembles is withdrawn. V2 explicitly states that dimension-free guarantees remain unproved for K > 1 and that exact small-ridge near-optimality conditions are not supplied. It also explains the fixed-bias variance advantage of enlarging models over adding ensemble members.

D1.justification: New Appendix F provides a repository link and states that all figure-generation code is publicly available. Conversely, v1's deep-network implementation appendix disappears, removing architecture, parameterization, augmentation, SGD, and early-stopping details. The retained RFRR implementation instructions largely match.

R1.justification: Remarks 5.2-5.3 and Section 7 newly position the finite-budget theorem against known infinite-ensemble/kernel equivalences, adding Dern, LeJeune, and Patil-related references. V2 also removes much of the maximal-update and feature-learning literature supporting the deleted deep experiments, substantially refocusing its research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the title, abstract, introduction, and preliminaries; separates 'More is Better' into its own section; and gathers near-optimality analyses into Section 6. Added formal remarks, expanded proof explanations, and a deterministic-equivalence appendix substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns, with extensive figure resizing and relocation. V2 adds the growth-exponent schematic as Figure 3, rearranges v1 Figure 4 into Figure 5, separates previously co-located supplementary figures, and removes the deep-network figures.

improvement.justification: V2 clarifies the limits of deterministic-equivalent guarantees, strengthens its explanation of novelty relative to prior work, and adds code-access information. However, it removes the entire deep-network validation and robustness suite without adding new empirical evidence. These gains in clarity and reproducibility documentation coexist with a substantial loss of empirical breadth, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
